svg.title: A parent calls to report that her 13-year-old, who started propylthiouracil 3 weeks ago for Graves disease, now has a temperature of 38.6 C and a sore throat. Which action should the nurse take first?
svg.desc: Fever and sore throat on an antithyroid drug means agranulocytosis until proven otherwise — stop the drug and get urgent evaluation with a CBC. Note that methimazole is preferred first-line in children because of PTU hepatotoxicity, but the agranulocytosis warning applies to both.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Endocrine & Metabolic
Read the situation
A parent calls to report that her 13-year-
old, who started propylthiouracil 3 weeks
ago for Graves disease, now has a
temperature of 38.6 C and a sore throat.
Which action should the nurse take first?
What fits here
Instruct her to hold the medication and
bring the child for urgent evaluation
Why it fits
Fever and sore throat on an antithyroid
drug means agranulocytosis until proven
otherwise — stop the drug and get urgent
evaluation with a CBC. Note that
methimazole is preferred first-line in
children because of PTU hepatotoxicity,
but the agranulocytosis warning applies to
both.
